added.name: Helios Intelligence
added.long_description:
Helios is building a molecular body test from a single drop of blood. Our at-home test measures more than 1,000 biomarkers and turns them into a living model of the body—designed to show what is happening now, surface risk earlier, and become more useful with every test.

By combining longitudinal molecular data with labs, wearables, health records, and outcomes, we are building toward a world model of human biology. Our goal is to simulate all of human health and use that intelligence to help people perform, recover, and live longer.
added.one_liner: At-home molecular body test: 1,000+ biomarkers from a drop of blood

added.name: Archgen Labs
added.long_description:
Archgen Labs builds AI-powered chip design tools for the next generation of 3D semiconductors.

Stacking compute vertically shortens connections and reduces the energy and delay of moving data. But it also makes heat harder to remove. Our tools help engineers optimize placement, timing, and temperature together so they can build faster, more power-efficient 3D chips.

Our GPU-accelerated placement engine ranked first in the Hudson River Trading macro-placement challenge. LayerTherm, our thermal analysis tool, predicts chip temperatures roughly 5,000× faster than conventional simulation in our benchmarks, helping engineers explore more designs and identify hotspots earlier. Newton, our AI chip design engineer, automates work across placement, routing, design-rule fixes, and timing closure.

We’re working with GlobalFoundries on 3D chip development, targeting our first tapeout in 2027.
added.one_liner: AI-powered EDA tools for faster, cooler 3D chips

added.name: Axonnic
added.long_description: Axonnic is building the missing data layer for dexterous robotics. Our wearable EMG technology captures human intent, effort and force directly from muscle activity as people demonstrate physical tasks. By revealing the physical signals that video cannot capture, Axonnic gives AI models the data they need to learn more precise and dexterous behaviour. Beyond robotics, this creates a foundation for new forms of human–computer interaction in which technology can understand and respond directly to human movement and intent.
added.one_liner: Bringing human dexterity to every robot

added.name: Superserve
added.long_description:
Traditional cloud infrastructure was built to run a single app for many users. Agents work differently. Each one needs its own isolated machine to write software on the fly, run tools and act on its own for hours or weeks. And everything it produces has to persist between sessions.

Superserve gives every agent and RL rollout its own virtual machine that starts in under 50ms. Machines start from templates with your repo and dependencies already loaded, pause with memory and files intact at zero compute cost, and resume or fork from that exact state. You can run docker, databases, browsers or any services on these VMs. 

API keys stay outside the machine and egress rules control what agents can reach.

For teams building coding agents, autonomous workers, or eval and training environments, that means elastic infrastructure with no servers or warm pools to manage, and control over what every agent can reach and which credentials it can see. 

We run over 100K machines (as of Oct 2026) every week for world-class teams, including Lindy, and Y Combinator itself.

As healthcare costs have increased, the patient's home has become incredibly important as a site of care. Yet, patients recovering at home are highly underserved.

long_description.after:
It costs nearly $12,000 for a patient to spend a single night at a hospital. Delivering care at home is often far less expensive and much more convenient for patients.

But robust infrastructure to enable this transition from the hospital to the home is missing. Instead, it’s a patchwork of different vendors, tied together by faxes, phone calls and hours of time by nurses. Durable medical equipment (DME) delivery is a part of healthcare that’s forgotten until it goes wrong.

Verse’s AI-enabled ordering platform solves these problems, ensuring patients and clinicians have a seamless experience every time.

We’re a well-funded Series C company backed by General Catalyst, SignalFire, and Sapphire Ventures, and we’re growing fast. If you want to help move healthcare from the hospital to the home, we’d love to meet you.

long_description.before:
We use AI and high-throughput mouse studies to discover therapeutics that modify neural activity in the brain. The initial focus is on epilepsies associated with autism and Parkinson’s disease with the potential to expand to any neurological disorder underlined by a dysfunction in neural activity. Our R&D is guided by AI models trained on high-density multimodal mouse data generated in-house.

We are 3 Oxford-trained neuroscientists supported by an experienced SAB from Harvard, Science Corp (ex-Neuralink), EPFL, Meta, and UCL.

In 1.5 months since landing in SF, we went from nothing to (1) opening and operating an animal lab in South SF, (2) obtaining a proof-of-concept in mice, (3) building a multimodal AI model that directs our screening approach and (4) submitting two provisional patents; all while utilizing less than 50% of our YC funding.
long_description.after:
We are developing therapies for disorders driven by dysfunctional neural circuits. To develop these therapies, we are building an agentic discovery platform that learns from experiments in our own in vivo lab.

Our agents use CircuitATLAS to connect disease phenotypes with the neural circuits, cell types and molecular mechanisms, identify therapeutic targets and design experiments to test them. Our cross-species models learn from large-scale neural activity data to identify conserved circuit states and help predict how an intervention’s effects may translate from preclinical models to humans.

At our Data Foundry in Manila, our team of RAs test these hypotheses in vitro and in vivo. The results refine our models and guide the next set of experiments. This lab-in-the-loop approach allows our agents to develop and test ideas against experimental evidence throughout discovery.

We are starting with epilepsy, with the goal of developing first-in-class therapies across a full spectrum of disorders driven by dysfunctional brain activity.

Publications:

- CircuitATLAS (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.09643). Target discovery platform which combines mechanistic reasoning with an in vivo lab-in-the-loop. AI agents identify therapeutic targets and design experiments that our research teams execute in the lab. The resulting biological data feeds back into the discovery process to iteratively refine hypotheses and validate new interventions.

- Cross species representation learning (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11222). Aligning mouse and human neural activity to predict clinical drug efficacy from preclinical data.

one_liner.before: AI drug discovery platform for neurotherapeutics
one_liner.after: Agentic platform for predictive neuro drug discovery + data foundry.

Each client implementation is a project in superglue, and its AI agents do the hands-on work across the whole project: the project plan from the kickoff, data assessment, fit-gap, configuration, data mapping and migration, testing, cutover and the integrations that run after go-live.

The agents execute the work in the client's systems, they don't just list what needs doing. Consultants review every change and sign off before anything reaches production. Approved migration scripts run the same way every time, with no AI at run time, and every run is logged.

superglue works with NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, Acumatica, SAP and about 140 other systems, and reads legacy sources such as QuickBooks Desktop, Sage 50 and 100, Dynamics GP, databases and files.

A Sage value-added reseller running 40 Sage Intacct implementations cut migration and configuration hours per project by 80%. superglue is SOC 2 Type II, offers EU data residency, and can be self-hosted.

one_liner.after: AI agents that run ERP implementations for consultants

long_description.before:
Everyone pays someone to handle the parts of their life that don't need them personally. The cleaner, the bookkeeper, the lawn service. Nobody could handle what lives in your phone. Until Blue.

Blue is a small USB-C dongle and iPhone app. Plug it in and say what needs doing. The follow-up you haven't sent, the appointment you haven't booked, the reply you owe. Blue opens the right app, does the work, and tells you when it's done. You don't touch your phone.

Works with every app already on your iPhone. 

The team brings complementary experience at scale: Omar Abdelaziz led Google Assistant’s transition to LLMs and holds one of earliest patents in LLM-based computer control; Peter Krogh spent decades designing voice-first dialog systems and was most recently a design lead at Google DeepMind building actions for Gemini Live; Muhammad Farhan Hossain helped ship Apple Vision Pro, is named on dozens of hardware/systems patents, and has led products from prototype to mass production.

We’ve built systems used by billions. Now we’re on to defining the next era of computing.
long_description.after:
AI changed coding when it got its own environment instead of a chat window. Developers stopped typing every line and started handing off whole tasks. The phone is next, and it needs the same rebuild.

Blue is that rebuild: a phone that’s also your chief of staff. It reads every notification, text, and email for you. Then it either handles each one and leaves you an FYI, or drafts a reply and waits for your OK. Anything else is one button away: say what needs doing, and Blue gets it done in the background, using the right apps.

It knows you from day one. Switch from your iPhone and Blue brings over your apps, messages, photos, and passwords, so it already knows who matters to you, how you write, and which card to use. No logins to hand over, no context to explain.

An app can’t do this; it takes owning the phone. Blue runs our own OS on Google Pixel today, with our own hardware in development. We sold out our first batch at YC’s Alumni Demo Day in September.

The team brings complementary experience at scale: Omar Abdelaziz led Google Assistant’s transition to LLMs and holds one of the earliest patents in LLM-based computer control; Peter Krogh spent decades designing voice-first dialog systems and before Blue was a design lead at Google DeepMind building actions for Gemini Live; Muhammad Farhan Hossain helped ship Apple Vision Pro, is named on dozens of hardware and systems patents, and has led products from prototype to mass production.

We’ve built systems used by billions. Now we’re building the phone that comes next.

one_liner.before: Your phone finally has someone to run it. Plug in Blue, just ask.
one_liner.after: AI rebuilt coding. We’re rebuilding the phone

long_description.before:
Knowledge work is being restructured by AI. Strategy happens in Claude. Research happens in ChatGPT. Building happens in Claude Code and Codex. Meetings get recorded, notes get written, agents run for hours and leave behind traces nobody reads. The people defining the next decade of work are already thinking with AI every day. But none of that thinking compounds. Every session starts from zero. The reasoning behind decisions, the context behind strategies, the evolution of ideas across hundreds of conversations - all of it evaporates.

Nessie is the infrastructure that makes it permanent. We auto-sync AI conversations and agent traces across every major provider - ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenClaw, Hermes, and more - alongside meetings, notes, and email from tools like Granola, Read AI, Plaud, and Obsidian. Everything a team produces with AI flows into one place and compounds over time.

Nessie turns that raw, heterogeneous data into an ontology: the live state of a company. Not a static schema but a continuously updated record of what the company knows, what it has decided, who owns what, and how its thinking has evolved, kept current as new work flows in. It is queryable from any agent through our CLI, MCP connector, and plugins, shareable across a team with real permissions, and deployable on-prem for organizations that need it.

Then the loop closes. Once a company’s state is legible to its agents, every agent run becomes training signal: which skills worked, which failed, which workflows keep repeating. Nessie feeds that signal back as reviewable improvements to the skills, prompts, and processes the team runs on. This is what makes a company recursive: its agents get better from its own history, the people working with them get better too, and the compounding never stops.

Where we are going: the AI-native organization runs thousands of agents that are powerful but amnesiac. Nessie is the layer that gives them, and the humans steering them, a shared memory. Science has journals, law has case law, software has git; AI-native knowledge work has had nothing. We are building it.

Founded by two Yale CS grads and former Amazon engineers, now a team of three in San Francisco. Backed by BoxGroup, Pioneer Fund, Y Combinator, Precursor, and more.

https://nessielabs.com

long_description.before:
TrueMile is building a fully autonomous logistics company, starting with trucking. Delayed pickups, empty miles and poor planning eat into a carrier’s profits. Our agents coordinate loads, routes, driver schedules and fuel stops to earn more from each truck and lower the cost of moving goods.

We’re starting with our own fleet so we control execution, learn from every delivery and keep the gains. Human drivers come first. As autonomous trucks become available on our routes, we’ll have the customers, freight and infrastructure ready for them.

As we drive toward AGI, people will still need groceries, clothes and materials to build their homes. Someone has to move all of it. We want every leap in AI to show up in what people pay for everyday goods.
long_description.after:
TrueMile is building an AI-native trucking company. We run our own fleet, using agents to find freight, plan loads, and coordinate drivers and brokers.

Our goal is to reduce empty miles, improve truck utilization, and lower the cost of moving goods. Operating the fleet ourselves lets us connect each decision to its outcome on the road and improve how we work.

We’re starting with human drivers. As autonomous trucks become available on our routes, we intend to put them to work within an established freight network.

Founder Harpreet Dhaliwal started running his family’s trucking business at 19 and has generated more than $7M in trucking revenue. The tools he built for that operation became TrueMile.

For recurring truckload freight and partnerships: harpreet@truemile.ai

Our focus is Macro and Rates Research and MBS, with munis, ABS and corporates next.
long_description.after: Oasive gives bond investors the data, models and research to decide what to buy. For muni credit analysts, Oasive brings a borrower's audited financials, debt, board meetings and local news into one page built around what matters for that sector, with every number linked to its source. Before a fund buys a bond from a city, school district, hospital or airport, that's the information its analyst has to dig up by hand from PDFs on local websites, board minutes and local news. We also serve agency MBS investors (collateral analytics, our own prepayment model and loan-level relative value) and rates investors (US and global macro with Treasury rich/cheap models).
